results.notes: Overall from the replication rating CSV, Day==2. Authors' Supplementary Material notebook read only as text; Tables S4/S7 use evaluation-level OLS with an intercept and both arm indicators, conventional SEs, and numeric DAT/Experience/Ability/English controls when adjusted. Source: PDF p. 48 (Table S4) or p. 51 (Table S7); reproduction sample: 1068 ratings, 267 people, arm counts {"Copilot": 90, "Human Confirmation": 85, "Human Creativity": 92}. Complete-case exclusion for the four baseline covariates removes four people (three Human Confirmation, one Human Creativity), or 16 ratings. Participant statistics use these same model-sample people. The four ratings of each person's single story are averaged within ID. Arm SDs use denominator n-1. The requested difference and HC2 SE come from a new, unadjusted two-arm OLS on those participant means, even when the slug names an adjusted published regression. Thus the raw difference need not equal the reproduced adjusted coefficient. HC2 is also checked against sqrt(treatment_sd^2/n_treatment + control_sd^2/n_control). Table 1 pooled statistics are used only to verify the data and are never used as arm statistics. Individual randomization among Day 2 AI modes (PDF p. 4). Day 1 was a fixed-order unassisted baseline, so round='all' denotes the single eligible Day 2 contrast; no paired or first_round result is applicable. Difference is treatment minus control in raw outcome units.

Set-level semantic similarity; original posted 3,072-dimensional text-embedding-3-large embeddings and the exact associated story texts are used, with no substitute model or regenerated embeddings. Recompute cosine(embedding_i, mean of all embeddings in its arm). This matches every saved Similarity value within 1e-12 and reproduces PDF p. 7 means and CIs; Figure 4 notebook cell 8 summarizes that saved Similarity column using a t interval over stories. IMPORTANT PROCEDURE DISCREPANCY: the average includes the focal story. The caption on PDF p. 16 incorrectly says 'other stories'. Its literal leave-one-out procedure gives Human Creativity=0.702021511789 and Copilot=0.736527840166, which do not match the printed values. This result reports the exact numerical measure implemented by the saved embeddings and similarities, not the caption's leave-one-out variant. Under rule 5, only the recomputed set measure, its descriptive difference, and the paper's arm CIs in reproduced are retained. These are raw cosine similarities; a positive difference means greater similarity. Shared stories/centroids create dependence. The paper's arm CIs are not contrast CIs and do not establish uncertainty at the level of randomization. treatment_sd, control_sd, difference_se, and se_type are null: there is no independent participant-level outcome or appropriate HC2/paired SE for this set measure. The text/genre corpus has 93 Human Creativity, 91 Human Confirmation, and 91 Copilot stories (275 Day 2 stories), plus 282 Day 1 stories. The rating CSV instead has 93, 88, and 90 Day 2 writers (271), plus 278 Day 1 stories, matching PDF p. 21. The paper does not print genre/embedding-specific arm counts, so 271 is not substituted for the separate text-analysis corpus. No exclusion can be inferred to reconcile the extra text rows: these CSVs contain unique full story texts but no writer IDs or link to the rating file. n_treatment/n_control for text analyses count unique stories under the paper's one-final-story-per-writer-per-day protocol (PDF pp. 4,18-20); this mapping cannot be independently checked by participant ID. All deposited text rows are retained as in the Figure 4 notebook, which reproduces the printed means and intervals. Individual randomization among Day 2 AI modes (PDF p. 4). Day 1 was a fixed-order unassisted baseline, so round='all' denotes the single eligible Day 2 contrast; no paired or first_round result is applicable. Difference is treatment minus control in raw outcome units.
